class.description: This is a test class to demonstrate how to create a class in Godot using C++. It contains a method that prints "Hello, World!" to the console and a property that can be set and get from the editor. The property is of type String and has a default value of "The beginning of something great".

method.name: say_hello
method.description: This method prints "Hello, World!" to the console when called. You can call this method from the editor or from another script to see the output in the console. To call this method from the editor, select the node that has this script attached and click on the "Call" button in the inspector. Then, type "say_hello" and press Enter. To call this method from another script, you can use the following code: ``` var test_node = get_node("path_to_your_node"); test_node.say_hello(); ``` Make sure to replace "path_to_your_node" with the actual path to the node that has this script attached. When you run the scene, you should see "Hello , World!" printed in the console. This is a simple example to demonstrate how to create a method in a C++ class for Godot and how to call it from the editor and from another script. Feel free to modify the method to do something more interesting or to add more methods to the class! Remember to compile your C++ code and reload the project in Godot to see the changes take effect.
